mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved for two consecutive weeks, from -28.0 to -20.4 percent below baseline with a t-1w peak of -17.9, as commuting routines return. Returning office workers restore weekday lunchtime and after-work retail trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved -28.0, -24.3, -17.9, -20.4 across the four weekly means, a net gain of 7.6 points
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below its trailing 28-day mean of -22.45 in the four weeks following any two-week WORKPLACES improvement of at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has slipped from a t-2w peak of +8.9 to +7.3, meaning households spend fewer daytime hours at home. This release of home-bound time converts into out-of-home retail trips, raising RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +7.5 percent above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from +8.9 at t-2w to +7.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: Following any week in which the RESIDENTIAL weekly mean prints below +7.5, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not higher than its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is the necessary condition for retail recovery: stores refill only when both commuting and discretionary transit trips return together. The concurrent moves (TRANSIT -15.3 to -14.6, WORKPLACES -28.0 to -20.4) should lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -16.0 while WORKPLACES weekly mean rises above -21.0 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -15.3 to -14.6 and WORKPLACES from -28.0 to -20.4 over the four weekly means
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT exceeds -16.0 and WORKPLACES exceeds -21.0 simultaneously, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is at or below its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS has stayed pinned between -34.1 and -31.4 for four weeks, a flat profile consistent with an end-of-summer seasonal collapse in outdoor leisure rather than a fresh policy shock. With outdoor recreation options shut off, discretionary spending rotates away from recreation-linked retail, pushing RETAIL_REC down over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS stayed within a 2.7-point band (-34.1 to -31.4) across all four weekly means
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than its trailing mean of -22.45 while PARKS remains below -30.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime, simultaneous declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signal that movement controls are being re-imposed rather than that demand is organically weak. Capacity limits and reduced trip chains then throttle RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT drops more than 3.0 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES drops more than 3.0 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell 1.2 points from t-1w (-13.4) to t-0w (-14.6) while WORKPLACES fell 2.5 points (-17.9 to -20.4)
failure_condition: In weeks meeting the joint dual-decline trigger, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days exceeds its trailing 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM spiking above +10 marks precautionary stockpiling and renewed household caution, a behavior that precedes withdrawal from discretionary trips. The t-1w print of +11.3 therefore predicts that RETAIL_REC softens within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean exceeds +10.0 percent above baseline
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached +11.3 at t-1w after +5.1 at t-2w, then eased to +9.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: The week immediately following any GROCERY_PHARM print above +10.0 shows RETAIL_REC at or above its level in the trigger week.

mechanism_narrative: A RESIDENTIAL decline coupled with a WORKPLACES rise is a home-to-office substitution signal: the same households that stop being home-bound for work also resume in-person shopping. The joint move predicts higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL eased from +8.9 to +7.3 while WORKPLACES rose from -24.3 to -20.4 over the last two weekly means
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL falls and WORKPLACES rises simultaneously, the next-28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the trailing 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has stalled rather than recovered: t-0w at -21.7 is below t-1w at -20.4 and the four-week mean of -22.45 is roughly flat, showing no self-sustaining momentum. Absent a new driver, that inertia carries the series sideways to lower over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly means are -23.0, -24.7, -20.4, -21.7, a net change of only +1.3 points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next 7 days exceeds -20.4, the t-1w level, contradicting the stalled-momentum claim.
